title: Help Center Performance and Latency Issues
content_summary: Guidance on troubleshooting slow API responses, page loads, and batch jobs in the Help Center product.
content_body: When users report slow response times or HTTP 504 errors, first check for CPU usage spikes or database query timeouts in the monitoring dashboard. Database contention is a frequent root cause, often requiring query optimization or capacity increases. If the issue is intermittent, investigate potential race conditions or known product limitations that may require an engineering escalation. For cases where performance matches expected baselines, confirm if the behavior is 'as designed' and provide relevant documentation to the user.

title: Funnel Analyzer: Troubleshooting Export Corruption and Duplicate Records
content_summary: Guidance on resolving common data issues in Funnel Analyzer exports, including truncated files, encoding errors, and duplicate records caused by idempotency failures or data quality gaps.
content_body: When users report truncated files or encoding errors in Funnel Analyzer exports, first verify the source data integrity and check for recent updates to the export service. Duplicate records often stem from idempotency/duplicate-processing failures during high-volume ingestion; reprocess the affected queue to clear stuck jobs. If data loss or severe corruption is confirmed, run the standard data repair script to restore consistency. For known product defects, apply the latest patch and use manual reconciliation as a temporary workaround while the fix propagates.

title: Session Controller: Troubleshooting Authentication Failures and Identity Provider Connectivity
content_summary: Provides a broad overview of common authentication issues within Session Controller, focusing on token acquisition, password reset workflows, and SSO redirect failures.
content_body: When users report access denied errors or missing MFA prompts, first verify the health of the connected Identity Provider. Token acquisition failures often stem from expired certificates or underlying product bugs related to token expiration handling. For password reset issues, confirm that the link expiration logic matches the SMTP server's delivery time; if emails are missing, check for duplicate account conflicts. In cases where standard certificate renewal or session resets do not resolve the issue, engage the vendor for a product patch assessment.

title: Troubleshooting Queue Manager Performance and Storage Issues
content_summary: General guidance for diagnosing high replication lag, disk exhaustion, and slow responses in Queue Manager environments, focusing on database contention and resource limits.
content_body: When Queue Manager exhibits slow response times or high replication lag, first check for database contention and connection pool exhaustion. If disk usage is critical or index corruption is detected, verify underlying infrastructure health and resource availability. Typically, these issues stem from resource exhaustion or hardware failures rather than application logic errors. Resolve capacity-related problems by provisioning additional storage or optimizing database indexes. For severe hardware failures, initiate a failover to secondary infrastructure and schedule replacement of affected nodes.

title: Missing localized strings and incorrect calculation totals in Mobile App
content_summary: Addresses localization defects where text is missing or calculation totals are wrong due to race conditions or known product limitations.
content_body: If localized text is missing or totals are incorrect, first check if the issue is reproducible in all languages or only specific ones. This often stems from a race condition during asset loading or a known product limitation regarding dynamic string injection. Verify the app version; if it is older than the latest patch, upgrade the client immediately. For persistent issues after updating, escalate to engineering with device logs. If confirmed as a known limitation, apply the standard workaround documented in the release notes.

title: Resolving HTTP 429 and Schema Mismatch in Customer Portal Webhooks
content_summary: Addresses cases where Customer Portal webhooks fail to fire, resulting in HTTP 429 errors and API schema validation failures due to dependency mismatches.
content_body: When webhook deliveries to the Customer Portal return HTTP 429 errors alongside schema validation failures, the issue is typically a dependency failure causing a schema mismatch in the Admin Console payload. First, check the Admin Console logs to confirm the specific schema version being sent versus what the receiving endpoint expects. If the schema is outdated, execute the recommended schema migration to align the API contract with the latest vendor standards. For persistent mismatches, engage the vendor to update the API contract definitions. Resolving the underlying dependency failure often clears the rate-limiting errors, as the system stops retrying invalid payloads.

title: Workaround for Elevated Privileges and Certificate Warnings During LDAP Credential Rotation
content_summary: Addresses known limitations in the LDAP Connector where credential rotation does not immediately propagate, causing transient elevated privileges, certificate warnings, and account lockouts.
content_body: During scheduled credential rotation, users may observe transient elevated privileges and certificate warnings, potentially leading to account lockouts. This is a known product limitation where the connector does not instantly propagate rotated credentials. Agents should reassure customers that this behavior is temporary and expected within the rotation window. No permanent fix is required as the system is working as designed; advise waiting for the propagation cycle to complete or manually triggering a connector sync if urgent.

title: Troubleshooting Webhook Engine TLS Connection Failures
content_summary: Addresses connection refusals, DNS lookup failures, and HTTP 504 errors caused by expired certificates or firewall misconfigurations in the Webhook Engine.
content_body: When Webhook Engine delivery fails with 'connection refused' or 'HTTP 504', check the target endpoint's certificate validity first, as expired TLS certs are a common root cause. Simultaneously, verify that no recent firewall rule changes are blocking the outbound connection or causing DNS lookup failures. Renew expired certificates immediately and update firewall allow-lists to restore connectivity.

title: Workaround for Missing UI Elements in Non-English Locales
content_summary: Addresses specific UI rendering issues and missing text when using the Data Export Service in non-English locales.
content_body: Users frequently report that certain UI buttons and labels fail to render when the application locale is set to German or Japanese. This occurs because the current string resource files are incomplete for these languages, a known limitation in version 2.4. As a temporary workaround, switch the interface language to English (US) to ensure all functional elements display correctly. Please escalate to Engineering if the issue persists after changing the locale, as a hotfix is currently in development.

title: Attribution Engine: Handling Upstream Rate Limits from Data Source V1
content_summary: Addresses third-party API unavailability and timeout errors caused by upstream rate limiting when using the legacy Data Source V1 connector. Provides steps for identifying vendor throttling and applying temporary backoff workarounds.
content_body: When the Attribution Engine receives timeout errors or 429 responses, check the raw logs for the upstream dependency to confirm rate limiting. This issue is most commonly triggered when the Data Source V1 API exceeds its concurrent request limit of 50 calls per minute. To resolve, implement a manual backoff strategy in the scheduler configuration until the vendor's capacity is restored. If the error persists, escalate to the vendor account manager to request a temporary quota increase or verify if the API key has been revoked.

title: Third-Party Dependency Failures in Subscription Manager
content_summary: General troubleshooting for notification delivery failures and upload timeouts caused by external vendor issues or expired credentials.
content_body: When users report undelivered notifications or file upload failures, first check the vendor status page for known incidents. If the vendor is operational, investigate our logs for specific HTTP errors like 401 (expired API key) or 429 (rate limiting). Clock skew between our systems and the vendor's can also cause signature validation failures, so verify NTP synchronization. For immediate mitigation, consider rotating credentials or enabling a fallback queue if the provider supports it. Escalate to engineering if the issue persists beyond vendor resolution windows.

title: Addressing Security Violations and Login Anomalies in Subscription Manager
content_summary: Guidance for diagnosing unexpected logouts, account lockouts, and certificate warnings caused by improper access reviews or credential rotation issues.
content_body: When users report unexpected logouts, account lockouts, or certificate warnings, first check the audit logs for missing entries or signs of elevated privileges, which may indicate a security policy violation. A common root cause is that credential rotation was not properly propagated across all nodes, or an improper access review left stale permissions active. To resolve this, perform a configuration change to ensure credentials are synchronized and update user permissions as needed. Finally, complete a thorough access review to confirm that all accounts are secure and compliant.

title: Secret Store: Remediation for Config Drift and Version Mismatches
content_summary: Addresses application crashes caused by version mismatches across environments during Secret Store deployments, specifically when an automatic rollback fails or leaves the system in an inconsistent state.
content_body: When a Secret Store deployment triggers an application crash due to config drift, verify that the active version matches the expected release across all environment nodes. If an automatic rollback was initiated but the system remains unstable, the rollback process may be incomplete, leaving residual configuration files or database entries from the failed release. Manually inspect the deployment logs to identify which specific components failed to revert. In cases of persistent instability, apply the latest available product patch to resolve known synchronization bugs. If patching does not restore stability, escalate to engineering with a copy of the drift report and recent deployment manifests.

title: Troubleshooting Feature Flag Application Issues in Deploy Manager
content_summary: Addresses scenarios where feature flags fail to apply or configuration changes do not take effect in Deploy Manager, often resulting in config drift alerts.
content_body: When a feature flag is not applying as expected in Deploy Manager, first verify that the configuration has been successfully committed and published. Check for any pending approval workflows that might be blocking the change from taking effect. Common causes include operator errors, such as selecting the wrong environment scope or targeting an inactive queue. Review the audit logs to identify recent configuration changes that may have caused drift. If the issue persists, confirm that the customer's access permissions are sufficient to modify the specific integration settings, as incorrect access levels can silently revert changes.

title: General Guidance on Provisioning and Onboarding Failures
content_summary: Provides a high-level troubleshooting framework for common provisioning issues such as sync stalls, bulk import failures, and missing welcome emails.
content_body: When encountering provisioning delays, first verify that the dependency services, particularly the Session Controller, are online and healthy. If the issue involves a bulk import failure, determine if the entire job failed due to data quality issues or if partial failures occurred due to specific record conflicts. For SSO Integration Module errors, check for customer configuration mismatches in the identity provider settings. Standard resolution involves running data repair scripts for corrupted records or engaging the vendor for deep dependency remediation. Always confirm with the customer that they have whitelisted the necessary email domains if welcome notifications are missing.

title: Triage: Intermittent Crashes and Data Mismatches Without Reproduction
content_summary: Guidance for handling tickets where application crashes or data mismatches cannot be reproduced, focusing on information gathering and operator error checks.
content_body: When facing intermittent issues with no clear reproduction steps, first verify if the incident correlates with specific operator actions or configuration changes. Check audit logs for manual edits that might have caused transient data mismatches or service instability. If the issue is not reproducible after initial investigation, provide the customer with self-service diagnostic tools and close the ticket as a duplicate or pending further information. Often, these cases are resolved by correcting a local configuration setting rather than a core software bug.

title: Troubleshooting Notification Hub Timeouts Due to Vendor API Deprecation
content_summary: Addresses Notification Hub delivery failures and timeouts caused by upstream vendor API deprecations or service outages.
content_body: Check the vendor status page to confirm if there is an active incident or recent deprecation notice affecting the API endpoint used by Notification Hub. If the vendor confirms a service failure, engage the vendor support team immediately to understand the remediation timeline. In the interim, enable the fallback delivery method configured in Notification Hub settings to prevent message loss. Document the error codes observed in the logs to assist the vendor in diagnosing the specific dependency failure.

title: Troubleshooting Cohort Builder notification failures due to upstream dependency timeouts
content_summary: Addresses cases where Cohort Builder notifications fail to deliver due to upstream service timeouts or errors, often linked to expired API keys or dependency failures.
content_body:
1. Check the Cohort Builder logs for upstream dependency timeouts or 5xx errors during the notification dispatch window.
2. Verify that the API keys for the downstream notification vendor are valid and have not expired.
3. If keys are valid, confirm the vendor's status page for any known outages or dependency failures.
4. Rotate credentials immediately if an expired key is identified.
5. If the issue persists, engage the vendor support team with specific request IDs for further remediation.

title: Resolving LDAP Connector Bulk Import Failures and Duplicates
content_summary: Addresses bulk import failures, duplicate account creation, and 'account not found' errors in LDAP Connector caused by operator misconfiguration or incomplete migrations.
content_body: When a bulk import fails completely or creates duplicates, first check the LDAP Connector schema mapping for operator errors, such as incorrect base DNs or filter attributes. Incomplete migrations often leave stale attributes that trigger 'account not found' errors for existing users. Run the data repair script to remove duplicate entries and reconcile orphaned records. Finally, apply the necessary configuration change or schema migration to align the connector with the current OAuth Service directory structure.

title: Token Service: Resolving Data Out-of-Sync and Corruption Issues
content_summary: Guidance for troubleshooting data mismatches, stale records, and encoding errors within the Token Service and Mobile App. Covers common causes like migration defects and duplicate processing failures.
content_body: When users report data loss or mismatches, first verify if a recent schema migration or incomplete data sync occurred. Encoding errors and duplicate records often stem from idempotency failures in the token generation queue. Check the Mobile App logs for truncated file indicators or stale cache entries that fail to refresh. Standard resolution involves running the provided data repair script or triggering a queue reprocessing event. If the issue persists across multiple users, apply the latest product patch to address known migration defects.

title: General Troubleshooting for SSO Certificate and Permission Errors
content_summary: Addresses common issues related to certificate warnings, account lockouts, and missing audit logs in the SSO Integration Module and Permission Engine.
content_body: Users often encounter certificate expiration warnings or access denied errors due to improper credential rotation. If audit logs are missing entries, check if the access review was completed correctly, as operator error can sometimes disrupt logging. For account lockouts following brute-force attempts, ensure that elevated privileges are managed via permission updates rather than hardcoded credentials. Typically, resolving these security policy violations requires a configuration change to propagate new certificates or rotate credentials across all nodes.

title: Token Service and Subscription Manager: Handling Database Contention and Index Corruption Due to Disk Exhaustion
content_summary: Troubleshooting guide for high replication lag and index corruption in Token Service and Subscription Manager databases caused by disk space exhaustion and contention. Covers immediate mitigation steps including capacity increases and data repair scripts.
content_body: When disk space is critically low, database contention can spike, leading to high replication lag and detected index corruption. Immediately increase storage capacity to relieve pressure on the I/O subsystem. Run the standard data repair script to rebuild corrupted indices; if indices fail to rebuild automatically, perform a manual index rebuild during a maintenance window. Check for data quality issues that may have triggered the corruption, such as malformed subscription records. Apply database optimization patches if the root cause is traced to inefficient query execution plans exacerbated by low disk space.

title: Troubleshooting Notification Hub Configuration Drift and Service Unresponsiveness
content_summary: Addresses service unresponsiveness and config drift in Notification Hub caused by unsupported settings or operator errors, requiring manual configuration alignment and access review.
content_body: When Notification Hub fails to apply new settings or reports drift, first verify that the configuration values are supported in the current product tier. Check for recent operator changes in the admin console or via API, as unsupported parameters often cause the service to become unresponsive. Resolve the issue by reverting to a known-good configuration state and enforcing the correct settings through a controlled change request. Conduct a thorough access review to identify which operator introduced the invalid configuration and provide targeted training to prevent recurrence.

title: Fixing HTTP 500 and Webhook Retries in Analytics Dashboard API due to Pagination Schema Mismatch
content_summary: Addresses malformed JSON responses and exhausted webhook retries caused by pagination bugs in the Analytics Dashboard API.
content_body: 1. Check API logs for HTTP 500 errors during high-volume data pulls, often triggered by a third-party service failure or timeout on the vendor side. 2. Verify that your integration handles pagination correctly; a mismatch in the expected schema (e.g., missing 'next_page' token) can break the loop and cause retries to exhaust. 3. Implement a temporary workaround by manually paginating with fixed limits to stabilize webhook delivery. 4. The permanent fix requires an API contract update from the vendor and a subsequent schema migration on your end to align with the corrected response structure. 5. Engage the vendor if the issue persists after applying the recommended schema adjustments.

title: General Billing Discrepancies and Proration Issues
content_summary: High-level overview of common billing errors such as proration miscalculations, currency conversion issues, and double charges, with general guidance on resolution paths.
content_body: Billing discrepancies often stem from configuration errors in the Subscription Manager or defects within the Billing Engine. Operators should first verify the customer's subscription state and recent changes to rule out manual entry errors. If the issue involves currency conversion or third-party payment gateway failures, engaging the vendor or escalating to engineering may be required. Common resolutions include applying product patches, adjusting configuration settings, or processing manual refunds via workaround.

title: Currency Converter Data Integrity and Corruption Resolution
content_summary: Guidance for diagnosing and resolving missing, duplicate, or corrupted data in Currency Converter exports resulting from migration defects or product bugs.
content_body: Data corruption in Currency Converter often stems from incomplete migrations or encoding mismatches that truncate export files. If users report missing records or duplicates, first verify the source schema and migration logs for errors. Standard resolutions include applying the latest product patch to address known defects or running a data repair script to reconcile discrepancies. For persistent issues, a full data re-sync is recommended to ensure alignment between internal records and external exports.

title: Rate Limiting Discrepancies in API Gateway (Legacy Config Flow)
content_summary: Addresses issues where rate limiter configurations do not apply or cause data mismatches, specifically when using the legacy global configuration method.
content_body: 1. Navigate to the API Gateway console and select the 'Global Settings' tab. 2. Under the 'Traffic Management' section, locate the legacy `enable_rate_limiting` boolean flag and ensure it is set to `true`. 3. Verify that the `requests_per_minute` integer value is not conflicting with any route-specific overrides. 4. If the feature flag fails to apply after 5 minutes, check the operator access logs to confirm the write permissions were not denied. 5. Revert to the previous known-good configuration snapshot if data mismatches persist, as the global flag may override individual route policies unexpectedly.

title: Token Service and Identity Vault: Fixing Scope Consent Mismatches
content_summary: Addresses scenarios where Token Service grants or denies access unexpectedly due to scope/consent mismatches in Identity Vault policies.
content_body: 1. Check the requested scopes in the Token Service logs against the consent policies in Identity Vault. 2. Look for policy misconfigurations where overly broad or restrictive scopes are applied incorrectly. 3. Verify if improper access reviews failed to update user roles or service permissions. 4. Correct the policy configuration in Identity Vault to align with the required access levels. 5. Initiate a fresh access review to ensure all permissions are accurate and compliant.

title: Troubleshooting Incorrect Calculations and UI Rendering Issues in Funnel Analyzer
content_summary: Addresses scenarios where Funnel Analyzer displays incorrect calculations due to UI rendering failures, broken sorting, or stale cache data.
content_body: When users report incorrect metrics or broken sorting in Funnel Analyzer, first check for a stale cache, which is the most common cause of display discrepancies. Clear the browser cache and session tokens to force a refresh of the calculation engine. If the issue persists and affects multiple users, verify if search results are returning incorrect data due to a known product defect. As a temporary workaround, guide the user to export raw data for manual verification. If the defect is confirmed, escalate to Engineering with specific query logs and screenshots of the rendering failure.

title: Addressing Audit Log Gaps in Identity Vault due to Retention Policy Limitations
content_summary: This note explains why audit log gaps or missing entries occur in Identity Vault when specific retention policies are applied, identifying it as a known product limitation.
content_body: Agents may observe missing audit log entries or gaps when configuring strict retention policies within Identity Vault. This behavior stems from a known product limitation where high-frequency events are occasionally dropped if the retention window conflicts with internal buffer thresholds. While the missing data is unrecoverable, this state is considered 'as designed' for the current version. To prevent future monitoring alerts from firing unnecessarily, update the alerting rules to ignore these specific gaps. A workaround involves adjusting the retention policy to a less aggressive timeframe, which stabilizes log ingestion.

title: Troubleshooting Intermittent 5xx and Failover Issues in Billing Disputes Handler and Notification Hub
content_summary: Addresses common reliability scenarios including container OOMKilled errors, intermittent 5xx responses, and failed failover events in core billing and notification services.
content_body: When agents encounter intermittent 5xx errors or full outages, first verify if the affected services are returning 503 status codes due to failing health checks. For Billing Disputes Handler, check for container OOMKilled events which often indicate a race condition or memory leak introduced by a bad deployment; immediate rollback is the standard resolution. If failover did not occur during an infrastructure hardware failure, engineering escalation is required to manually execute failover or replace the underlying hardware. Notification Hub issues with intermittent failures should be triaged for potential product patches if the root cause is identified as a known software defect.

title: API Gateway Upgrade Issues: Version Mismatch and Canary Failures
content_summary: Guidance on troubleshooting API Gateway deployments where upgrades result in version mismatches, canary stalls, or application crashes due to incomplete migrations or operator errors.
content_body: When upgrading the API Gateway, ensure all environment configurations are synchronized to prevent version mismatches that trigger application crashes. If a canary rollout stalls, check for feature flag propagation delays or migration script errors in the logs. Incomplete database migrations often cause breaking changes; run a data repair script or execute the pending schema migration if detected. Operator errors during deployment configuration are a frequent root cause, so review recent changes before initiating a rollback. If a bad deployment is confirmed, immediate rollback is the safest resolution, followed by customer education on proper upgrade procedures.

title: Fixing Pagination and Layout Bugs in Attribution Engine Workflow
content_summary: Guidance on troubleshooting broken pagination and UI misalignment in the Attribution Engine workflow caused by race conditions or product defects.
content_body: 1. If pagination controls fail to load or UI elements appear misaligned during the workflow steps, check for known product defects in the current release version. 2. This issue is often triggered by a race condition where localized text loads slower than the container, causing a layout shift. 3. As a temporary workaround, agents should advise users to zoom out (Ctrl + -) to force a re-render of the UI elements. 4. If the workaround fails, escalate to engineering with a screenshot and the exact step where the UI breaks.

title: API Gateway Canary Release Failures: Handling Rollbacks and Flag Issues
content_summary: Troubleshooting steps for failed canary deployments in API Gateway, focusing on feature flag application issues and version incompatibilities.
content_body:
1. Check the deployment logs for 'operator error' or specific version mismatch warnings.
2. If the feature flag fails to apply, verify the version compatibility between the API Gateway instance and the current deployment artifact.
3. Initiate an immediate rollback if the canary deployment triggers a failure state.
4. Conduct an access review to ensure the operator had the correct permissions for the flag configuration.
5. Educate the customer on the new version requirements to prevent recurrence.

title: Troubleshooting Session Controller Notification Failures Due to Expired API Keys
content_summary: Addresses upstream dependency timeouts and notification delivery failures in the Session Controller caused by expired API keys or vendor-side dependency issues.
content_body: When Session Controller notifications fail to deliver, check the upstream dependency logs for 401 Unauthorized errors or timeout exceptions. These symptoms typically indicate that the associated API key has expired or the third-party vendor is experiencing degraded service. To resolve, immediately rotate the expired credentials in the secure vault and restart the Session Controller service. If the issue persists after credential rotation, engage the vendor support team to investigate potential dependency failures on their end.

title: KPI Tracker: Resolving Duplicate Records and Garbled Text in Export Files
content_summary: Troubleshooting steps for corrupted CSV or Excel exports from KPI Tracker caused by migration defects or data quality issues.
content_body: If you encounter duplicate rows or garbled characters in a KPI Tracker export, first verify that the source data is not already duplicated within the application. Check the system logs for recent data migration jobs or bulk imports, as these often introduce encoding errors or stale entries. Run the standard 'Data Repair Script' to normalize character encoding and remove obvious duplicates. If the issue persists, initiate a 'Data Re-sync' between the source database and the KPI Tracker instance. For critical reporting, perform a 'Manual Reconciliation' against the source of truth before finalizing the export.

title: Troubleshooting HTTP 403 Errors and Wrong Data Visibility in Identity Vault Conditional Access
content_summary: Addresses HTTP 403 access denials and incorrect data visibility caused by misconfigured conditional access policies or incomplete access reviews.
content_body:
1. Verify the conditional access policy configuration for the affected user group to identify if the block was intentional or a misconfiguration.
2. Check if an improper access review was recently completed or if pending reviews have lapsed, which often triggers automatic denials or visibility changes.
3. Confirm that the user's current permissions align with the intended scope of the policy to resolve the 'wrong data' symptom.
4. Apply the necessary permission updates or policy corrections in Identity Vault to restore appropriate access levels.
5. Document the change and notify stakeholders once the configuration change has been validated.

title: Troubleshooting Connectivity and TLS Failures in Billing Services
content_summary: Guidance for diagnosing network partitions, proxy issues, and TLS handshake failures affecting Chargeback Handler and Fee Analyzer.
content_body: When users report HTTP 502 or 504 errors alongside service unresponsiveness, first verify DNS resolution is not failing. If certificates are expired, the connection may timeout or show warnings during the TLS handshake, requiring immediate certificate renewal. Check for infrastructure hardware failures if the issue persists across multiple nodes, as this may necessitate a failover or component replacement. Incorrect DNS configuration often mimics network partitions, so ensure all records point to the active service endpoints.

title: Rate Limiter ignores feature flag changes due to stale environment variable cache
content_summary: Troubleshoots scenarios where the Rate Limiter service remains unresponsive to configuration updates or feature flags because the underlying environment variable is not refreshing correctly.
content_body: If the Rate Limiter is not applying new feature flags or configuration changes, first verify that the relevant environment variable is correctly set in the deployment manifest. A common root cause is a policy misconfiguration where the variable is defined but not mapped to the service container's runtime environment. Check the pod or container logs for initialization errors related to `RATE_LIMITER_FLAGS`. To resolve this, ensure the configuration change is propagated by restarting the service or correcting the policy binding. Customer education should emphasize that environment variables are read at startup and do not support hot-reloading without a restart.

title: Workaround: Missing Onboarding Wizard Steps in Firefox
content_summary: Addresses reports of the Onboarding Wizard skipping steps or returning incorrect search results specifically in Firefox due to a known race condition.
content_body: Users may encounter inconsistent behavior where the Onboarding Wizard fails to load subsequent steps or displays incorrect search results in Firefox. This is caused by a known product limitation related to a race condition during initial script loading. As a temporary workaround, agents should advise users to clear their browser cache and disable any ad-blocking extensions before retrying. Engineering has escalated this issue for a future product patch to resolve the underlying timing conflict.

title: Token Expiration Bug Causing Duplicate Accounts and MFA Failures
content_summary: Resolves issues where Admin Console token expiration handling creates duplicate accounts or rejects MFA codes during SSO attempts.
content_body: If you see duplicate accounts created or MFA codes rejected in the Admin Console, check for SSO error pages indicating token expiration handling bugs. This is often caused by a specific bug in how tokens expire rather than an identity provider outage. The primary resolution is to apply the latest product patch. If the issue persists, perform a token/session reset or engage the vendor for further analysis.

title: Handling Intermittent Unreproducible Issues and Duplicate Tickets
content_summary: Guidance on managing tickets with insufficient information, operator errors, or duplicate reports across various products.
content_body: Many support tickets are opened for intermittent failures, slow responses, or browser inconsistencies that cannot be reliably reproduced. These often stem from operator error, unsupported configurations, or are simply duplicates of existing issues. Verify if the ticket is a duplicate and close it if so. Provide customer education on correct usage and perform an access review if data mismatches are suspected. If root cause cannot be determined, document the inability to reproduce and close the ticket.

title: UI Rendering Defects and Form Submission Failures in Help Center
content_summary: Troubleshooting steps for misaligned elements, white screens, or broken sorting in the Help Center due to cache or product defects.
content_body: If Help Center users report white screens, misaligned UI, or broken filtering, first clear the browser cache. Stale cache is a common cause of these rendering issues. If the problem persists, check if the feature is missing after a recent release, which may indicate a product defect or known limitation. Apply known-issue workarounds if available, or escalate to engineering for a permanent fix. No fix is required if the behavior is determined to be 'as designed'.

title: Resolving Billing Discrepancies and Subscription Renewal Failures
content_summary: Addresses overcharges, incorrect proration, and duplicate charges in the Chargeback Handler through reconciliation or configuration changes.
content_body: For issues like duplicate charges, incorrect proration, or refunds not reflecting in the Chargeback Handler, first verify if the cause is operator error or a data quality issue. Manual reconciliation or running a data repair script often resolves these discrepancies. If the problem is a product defect, escalate to engineering. For persistent configuration-related billing errors, adjust the subscription settings. Always complete an access review before closing high-value billing tickets.

title: Third-Party API Timeouts in Data Export and Notification Hub
content_summary: Solutions for HTTP 500 errors and rate limit issues caused by third-party service failures or breaking API changes.
content_body: When Data Export Service or Notification Hub encounters timeouts or HTTP 500 errors, check if a third-party service is down or if an API contract change has occurred. Rate limits may be exceeded if the upstream provider is failing to respond correctly. Engage the vendor to confirm service status or breaking changes. Apply a workaround to retry requests or adjust timeouts, and escalate for an API contract fix if the dependency's behavior is non-standard.

title: Database Contention and Replication Lag in Metrics Engine
content_summary: Troubleshooting high latency, timeouts, and backup failures in Metrics Engine and Config Manager due to resource exhaustion.
content_body: If Metrics Engine or Config Manager experiences slow queries, high replication lag, or failed backups, investigate database contention and resource exhaustion. Check disk usage and query performance metrics. Capacity increases or database optimization tasks like index rebuilds are common resolutions. For data quality issues causing delays, run a data repair script or adjust rate limits. Manual reconciliation may be required for critical data mismatches.

title: Handling Canary Release Failures and Config Drift in Secret Store
content_summary: Procedures for resolving application crashes and version mismatches after failed deployments or rollbacks in Secret Store.
content_body: When Secret Store deployments result in application crashes, version mismatches, or stalled canary rollouts, check for incomplete rollbacks or bad deployments. Operator error during migration script execution is a frequent root cause. Roll back the deployment to a stable version immediately. If configuration drift is detected, apply necessary configuration changes or engage engineering for a product patch. Always verify the state of the environment after a rollback.

title: Deprecation Issues with Tax Calculator and Currency Converter APIs
content_summary: Guidance for handling timeouts and upstream errors when third-party vendor APIs for tax or currency services are deprecated or failing.
content_body: If Tax Calculator or Currency Converter services show timeouts or upstream dependency errors, check the vendor status page for incidents or deprecation notices. These issues are typically caused by third-party service failures or deprecated API endpoints. Engage the vendor to confirm deprecation timelines. Implement a workaround by switching to an alternative endpoint or pausing the service until a dependency remediation plan is established.

title: High Latency and Batch Job Slowness in Report Builder
content_summary: Solutions for HTTP 504 errors and CPU spikes in Report Builder caused by capacity limits or race conditions under load.
content_body: Report Builder may exhibit high latency, HTTP 504 timeouts, or CPU spikes during batch jobs or heavy load. These symptoms often point to capacity limitations or race conditions in the database layer. Increase capacity resources or adjust query timeouts as a workaround. For persistent issues, escalate to engineering for a product patch or infrastructure replacement. Check if third-party dependencies are contributing to the latency before proceeding.

title: Managing Duplicate Tickets for Intermittent Crashes
content_summary: Steps to identify and close duplicate tickets reporting intermittent application crashes or data mismatches without clear root cause.
content_body: When multiple tickets report intermittent application crashes or data mismatches without reproducible steps, check for duplicates. These are often caused by operator error or insufficient information. Close the duplicate tickets after linking them to the primary issue. Perform an access review if data integrity is in question. Escalate to engineering only if a specific pattern or reproducible case emerges from the consolidated reports.

title: Triage: Intermittent Failures and Data Mismatches with Insufficient Logs

title: Resolving TLS Handshake Errors in Cache Service
content_summary: Specific troubleshooting steps for Cache Service connectivity issues caused by expired certificates or firewall misconfigurations resulting in TLS handshake errors and service unresponsiveness.

4. Update firewall configurations to allow proper TLS negotiation, then restart the Cache Service client connection.
