Check for identity provider outages if token acquisition fails or password reset emails are missing. For MFA prompts not appearing or codes being rejected, ensure the connector's time synchronization is correct and review customer configuration settings. Most issues resolve through configuration changes, customer education, or resetting the token/session. Engage the vendor if the root cause is an operator error within the identity provider's management interface.

title: Troubleshooting Subscription Renewal Failures and Duplicate Charges with Tax/Currency Tools
content_summary: Addresses issues where subscription renewals fail, resulting in duplicate charges, undercharges, or incorrect invoices due to misconfiguration in Tax Calculator or Currency Converter integrations.
content_body: When customers report double-billing or unexpected invoice totals, verify if the Tax Calculator or Currency Converter is applied multiple times in the renewal workflow. Most incidents stem from customers enabling these tools alongside a legacy billing rule, causing operator or configuration errors. Review the active subscription plan's billing cycle and ensure the currency conversion step is configured to run only once per transaction. Correct the configuration settings to remove the duplicate logic and provide documentation to the customer on how to properly set up these integrations for future renewals.

title: Handling Upstream Dependency Outages and Third-Party Service Failures
content_summary: Guidance on identifying and mitigating issues caused by external service outages, dependency timeouts, or credential failures affecting Subscription Manager.
content_body: When users report file upload failures or SMS delivery issues, first check the vendor status pages for known incidents. Verify if the Subscription Manager logs show timeout or error responses from upstream dependencies. Common causes include expired API keys or temporary vendor service degradation. Engage the vendor's support team immediately if a widespread outage is suspected. Implement workarounds such as queuing requests or rotating credentials if the root cause is internal configuration.

title: Workaround for OAuth Token Endpoint 504 Timeouts
content_summary: Instructions for bypassing webhook retry failures caused by third-party API contract changes resulting in empty responses or timeouts.
content_body: When the Token Service receives empty responses or 504 timeouts from the third-party provider, webhook retries will exhaust quickly. This issue was common before the v2 API contract update when the provider deprecated synchronous token issuance. To mitigate this, temporarily increase the client-side timeout threshold to 30 seconds and implement a manual queue for failed webhooks. Vendor engagement is required for a permanent API contract fix, but this workaround prevents immediate data loss.

title: Troubleshooting Feature Flag Failures and Migration Errors after Upgrade
content_summary: Addresses post-upgrade issues in Deploy Manager where feature flags fail to apply or migration scripts error out, typically caused by version incompatibility or operator mistakes.
content_body: Check the Deploy Manager version against the Queue Manager compatibility matrix to ensure no breaking changes were introduced. Verify that migration scripts executed without errors in the operator console; if they failed, inspect the logs for specific permission or schema mismatch issues. If the deployment was performed manually, review the operator's runbook adherence, as skipped steps often cause feature flag propagation delays. For immediate resolution, rollback to the previous stable version if business continuity is critical, then plan a controlled version upgrade after validating the migration path. Educate the customer on required pre-upgrade access reviews to prevent recurrence.

title: Troubleshooting Billing Discrepancies and Refund Delays
content_summary: Covers common causes for invoice errors, currency conversion issues, and refund delays. Includes guidance on verifying customer configuration and identifying potential product defects.
content_body: When customers report billing discrepancies, first verify their account configuration and tax settings to rule out customer-side errors. Check the Billing Disputes Handler logs for any recent operator actions or product defect alerts related to currency conversion. If a refund appears unprocessed, confirm the transaction status in the Invoice Service before assuming a failure. For overcharges or double billing, cross-reference the subscription ID with recent renewal events to identify configuration overlaps. Document any known issues with tax calculation logic if the root cause is determined to be a product defect.

title: Resolving Authorization Errors and Permission Propagation Delays
content_summary: Addresses HTTP 401 errors, role application failures, and data visibility issues. Focuses on identifying configuration errors and policy misconfigurations within the Permission Engine.
content_body: Start by checking the Permission Engine audit logs to determine if the user's role was applied correctly after assignment. If a user sees wrong tenant data, verify that their scope and consent settings match the intended access level. Permissions propagation delays can often be resolved by forcing a token refresh or waiting for the next cache sync cycle. Review any recent policy changes that might have inadvertently removed elevated privileges or restricted data access. Provide customers with documentation on proper role assignment procedures to prevent future configuration errors.

title: Fixing Corrupted Export Files from Event Tracker and Metrics Engine
content_summary: Specific guidance for handling garbled characters or stale data in export files. Details the use of repair scripts and data re-sync procedures to resolve corruption.
content_body: If an export file from the Event Tracker contains garbled characters, it is likely due to a data migration defect or quality issue during the extraction process. Run the standard data repair script provided for the Metrics Engine to sanitize the corrupted records. After repair, perform a data re-sync to ensure the source database reflects the corrected state. Verify the output by comparing a sample of records against the live dashboard to confirm accuracy. If manual reconciliation is required, document the specific field discrepancies for the engineering team.

title: Handling Exposed Credentials and Access Review Failures
content_summary: Addresses symptoms like certificate expiration warnings and unexpected access denials linked to credential exposure. Outlines steps for completing access reviews and applying workarounds.
content_body: When a certificate expired warning is accompanied by access denied errors, check if the credential was improperly rotated during a recent access review. If the issue stems from a known product limitation in the Role Manager, apply the documented workaround for permission updates. Ensure that any elevated privileges observed are legitimate and not a result of the exposed credential. Complete a fresh access review to revoke any stale or compromised tokens before re-provisioning access. Confirm that the new credential is properly stored in the secure vault to prevent recurrence.

title: Troubleshooting MFA Failures and Account Lockouts
content_summary: Focuses on resolving issues where MFA prompts do not appear or accounts are locked out. Guides agents on checking identity provider status and resetting sessions.
content_body: First, verify if the user's identity provider is experiencing an outage, which can cause MFA Manager to fail silently. If the MFA prompt is not appearing, check for unsupported browser configurations that might block the authentication flow. To resolve unexpected session expirations, reset the user's token and instruct them to clear their browser cache. For account lockouts, review the failed attempt logs to distinguish between brute-force attacks and simple user error. Engage the vendor if the issue persists after configuration changes and customer education steps.

title: Resolving Issues Caused by Incorrect Environment Variables
content_summary: Specific guide for diagnosing config drift and data mismatches stemming from missing or incorrect environment variables. Details policy correction and configuration change steps.
content_body: If Deploy Manager reports config drift, compare the current environment variables against the approved policy baseline to identify discrepancies. Missing environment variables often lead to data mismatch errors in downstream services, so check the startup logs for initialization failures. Update the incorrect variable in the configuration store and trigger a redeployment to apply the change. If the configuration is unsupported, consult the product documentation for valid parameter ranges. Educate the customer on proper variable management to prevent future drift.

title: Addressing UI Rendering Issues and Functional Defects in Feedback Collector
content_summary: Covers symptoms like broken sorting, misaligned elements, and incorrect calculations. Provides steps for cache clearing and identifying product defects or limitations.
content_body: When users report that sorting or filtering is broken, first instruct them to clear their browser cache, as stale data often causes UI rendering issues. If calculations show wrong totals, verify that the Feedback Collector version is up to date to rule out a known product defect. For missing feature functionality after a release, check the feature flag configuration to ensure the feature is enabled for the tenant. If UI elements are misaligned, determine if this is a known product limitation related to specific screen resolutions. Apply a workaround or product patch if the issue is confirmed as a bug rather than a configuration error.

title: Resolving Scope/Consent Mismatches in Data Export and Attribution
content_summary: Addresses incorrect access grants or denials due to scope mismatches. Details policy corrections and permission updates for the Data Export Service and Attribution Engine.
content_body: If a user is denied access or granted incorrect access to the Data Export Service, audit their scope and consent settings against the required permissions. For the Attribution Engine, ensure that the API client's consent scope matches the requested data access level to prevent wrong tenant data visibility. Update the policy configuration to align the scopes with the intended use case. After correcting the configuration, force a permission update to propagate the changes immediately. Verify that the access review process was completed successfully to rule out stale permission grants.

title: Managing Exposed Credentials and Audit Log Gaps in Data Pipeline
content_summary: Specific guidance for issues involving missing audit entries and elevated privileges linked to credential exposure. Covers access review completion and known-issue workarounds.
content_body: When audit log entries are missing for the Data Pipeline, check if an exposed credential caused authentication failures that bypassed logging. If elevated privileges are observed, immediately rotate the affected credentials and complete a thorough access review. Apply the known-issue workaround for permission updates if the system is not automatically revoking stale sessions. Ensure that the access control policies are correctly configured to prevent unauthorized elevation. Document the incident as a security event and verify that no data exfiltration occurred during the gap.

title: Resolving Replication Lag and Database Deadlocks
content_summary: Addresses symptoms like deadlocks and connection pool exhaustion caused by replication lag. Details data repair scripts and capacity adjustments for Feedback Collector and Data Export Service.
content_body: If database deadlocks are detected, check for replication lag between primary and secondary nodes that may be causing write conflicts. For the Feedback Collector, verify if index corruption is contributing to the performance degradation and run the data repair script if necessary. Increase the database connection pool capacity if exhaustion errors persist during peak load. Use manual reconciliation to resolve any data quality issues resulting from the lag. Adjust rate limits on the Data Export Service to reduce pressure on the database during replication catch-up.

title: Troubleshooting Elevated Privileges and Certificate Warnings in OAuth Service
content_summary: Addresses scenarios where users observe elevated privileges, certificate warnings, and account lockouts. This usually stems from credential rotation not being propagated or operator error.
content_body: When you see elevated privileges alongside certificate warnings and account lockouts in the OAuth Service, start by checking the credential propagation status. This often happens when a recent credential rotation fails to sync across all services. If the issue persists, review operator logs for potential configuration errors. The standard resolution involves performing a manual credential rotation and ensuring the configuration change is applied correctly.

title: Resolving Stalled Canary Rollouts and Version Mismatches in Deploy Manager
content_summary: Addresses canary rollout stalls caused by migration script errors and version incompatibilities, detailing steps to align environment versions and execute safe rollbacks.
content_body: When a canary rollout stalls with migration script errors, first verify that the target version is compatible with the current database schema. A common root cause is operator error leading to version mismatches across staging and production environments. To resolve, pause the rollout and compare version strings in the Deploy Manager dashboard. If the mismatch is critical, initiate a rollback to the last stable release using the rollback workflow. After restoring stability, review the migration scripts and upgrade the version consistently across all environments before retrying.

title: VPN Connectivity Failures with TLS Handshake Errors
content_summary: Resolves VPN connection failures characterized by TLS handshake errors and connection refused messages, typically caused by expired certificates or infrastructure hardware issues.
content_body: This issue often presents as an inability to establish a secure tunnel, resulting in TLS handshake failures and subsequent connection refusals. Begin by validating the certificate expiration date on the edge node; expired certs are a common root cause requiring immediate renewal. If the certificate is valid, check the underlying infrastructure hardware for signs of failure, as degraded components can disrupt the TLS negotiation process. Historical resolutions involved manual certificate renewal followed by a failover to secondary nodes, though modern infrastructure replacement is now preferred for hardware faults. Ensure the Cache Service configuration points to the updated certificate path after renewal to prevent persistent connection errors.

title: Handling Proration and Invoice Discrepancies in Subscription Manager
content_summary: Legacy guidance for investigating proration errors, invoice discrepancies, and currency mismatches. This document reflects the pre-2022 billing engine architecture and should be used for historical context or archived cases only.
content_body: When a customer reports an overcharge or incorrect proration, first verify the manual adjustment queue in the admin console, as the automated proration service previously failed to sync with these entries. Check the currency conversion logs under Settings > Billing > Legacy Rates, since the system used fixed daily rates that often caused discrepancies during high volatility. If a refund is not reflected, confirm that the manual reconciliation script was executed; automated refunds did not post to the ledger in this version. For stuck payments, escalate to engineering for a database rollback of the transaction lock, as the UI retry button was non-functional for timed-out sessions. Always educate customers that chargeback notices triggered an immediate suspension of the account until manual review was completed.

title: General Guidance on Authentication and Session Management Issues
content_summary: High-level troubleshooting procedures for common identity errors including unexpected logouts, MFA failures, and password reset issues.
content_body: When users report unexpected logouts or 'access denied' errors, first verify that the Session Controller is configured correctly. Check for known issues with the Identity Vault provider outage or token expiration handling bugs. If MFA prompts are missing or codes are rejected, ensure the user's device supports the current configuration. For expired password reset links, confirm email delivery services are functioning as expected. Most of these issues are resolved through configuration changes or customer education on best practices.

title: Token and SSO Authentication Failures
content_summary: Addresses unexpected logouts, premature token expirations, MFA prompt failures, and SSO redirect loops caused by IdP issues or configuration mismatches.
content_body: Authentication failures in the Token Service and Permission Engine typically stem from an Identity Provider (IdP) outage or unsupported federation configurations. Check the current status of your IdP and validate that your federation metadata matches the application settings exactly. If the issue persists, perform a token or session reset and review the application's authentication policies for unsupported settings. Engage the vendor if configuration changes do not resolve SSO redirect loops, and educate customers on avoiding manual clearing of session data during MFA prompts.

title: Troubleshooting Intermittent 5xx and Failover Issues in Cache Service
content_summary: Guidance for resolving intermittent 5xx errors, service unresponsiveness, and failed failover events in Cache Service, typically caused by dependency failures or bad deployments.
content_body: If monitoring reports a full outage or service unresponsive with no failover, first check recent changes in Config Manager. A bad deployment or dependency failure is the usual culprit when failover logic doesn't execute as expected. Verify that the downstream dependency is healthy; if it's failing, escalate to the vendor for dependency remediation. If the issue correlates with a recent release, perform a rollback immediately. Apply any available product patches to Cache Service if the root cause is identified as a known bug.

title: Troubleshooting Notification Hub Configuration Conflicts and Environment Variables
content_summary: Guidance on resolving configuration drift, conflicting settings, and environment variable issues in Notification Hub.
content_body: Check for conflicting configuration settings or default values that have not been properly overridden in the current environment. Data mismatches and unresponsive services often stem from policy misconfigurations or unsupported configuration types. Verify that all required environment variables are correctly applied, particularly for feature flags. If the issue persists, review your internal documentation for staleness, as outdated guides can lead to incorrect configuration changes. Typically, this is resolved by applying a direct configuration change or correcting the underlying policy.

title: Troubleshooting HTTP 403 and Wrong Tenant Data in MFA Manager
content_summary: Addresses issues where users receive HTTP 403 errors or see data from an incorrect tenant due to conditional access blocks in MFA Manager.
content_body: When users report seeing wrong tenant data or receiving HTTP 403 errors, first verify the conditional access policy assignments within the MFA Manager console. These issues are typically caused by policy misconfigurations or incomplete access reviews that fail to update user group memberships. To resolve, correct the underlying policy settings and ensure a recent access review has been completed to synchronize permissions. After applying the configuration change, ask the user to clear their cache and log in again to confirm the data visibility is restored to the correct tenant.

title: Troubleshooting Deployment Failures and Rollbacks in Load Balancer and Secret Store
content_summary: Guidance for diagnosing application crashes, migration errors, and version mismatches following deployments or upgrades to Load Balancer and Secret Store.
content_body: When a deployment fails or triggers a rollback, first check the migration logs for script errors which often indicate version incompatibilities. Verify that environment variables and feature flags match the expected schema for the target version, as operator errors in configuration are a frequent cause of post-deploy crashes. If a version mismatch is detected across environments, an incomplete rollback may be the root cause; ensure all nodes are reverted to the stable baseline. For persistent issues, escalate to engineering with detailed logs, and consider a configuration change or forced version upgrade once the incompatibility is isolated.

title: Legacy Intermittent Failures in Custom Configurations
content_summary: Addresses intermittent service unresponsiveness and data mismatches caused by unsupported configurations in legacy environments.
content_body: When users report intermittent failures or data discrepancies, verify if the environment uses a non-standard or unsupported configuration. These issues often stem from operator errors during setup that bypassed validation checks in earlier versions. The resolution typically involves guiding the customer to revert to supported settings and providing educational resources on configuration best practices. Note that newer platform updates may now prevent these configurations entirely.

title: Troubleshooting Third-Party Integration Failures
content_summary: Broad guidance for resolving notification, upload, and SMS delivery failures linked to upstream dependencies or API issues.
content_body: 1. Check the status page for known vendor outages or rate limiting alerts. 2. Verify API keys are valid and not expired; rotate credentials if necessary. 3. Ensure server clocks are synchronized to prevent timestamp validation errors. 4. If the issue persists, escalate to engineering for dependency remediation or engage the vendor directly. Always confirm configuration changes are propagated to the mobile app backend.

title: Resolving Failed Deployments with Deploy Manager
content_summary: Specific steps for handling feature flag failures and migration script errors following a version upgrade.
content_body: If features are missing or breaking changes occur post-upgrade, first check for version incompatibilities in the deployment logs. Operator errors during manual configuration adjustments are also common causes. To resolve, perform a rollback to the previous stable version if immediate service impact is observed. Once stable, conduct an access review and upgrade to the corrected patch version, ensuring the customer understands the new feature flag behavior.

title: Event Tracker Accessibility and Localization Defects
content_summary: Investigation guide for blank screens and missing localization text caused by product defects or race conditions.
content_body: Users reporting missing localization text or blank screens after a release may be encountering a race condition in the Event Tracker initialization. This is often a product defect rather than a configuration issue. Immediate action involves escalating to engineering for a hotfix or providing a known-issue workaround. Once a patch is released, guide customers to update to ensure accessibility compliance and correct text rendering.

title: Security Incident Response: Subscription Manager
content_summary: Procedures for addressing account lockouts and audit log gaps related to certificate issues and operator errors.
content_body: If elevated privileges are observed or audit logs appear incomplete, first check for expired certificates which may cause authentication failures and lockouts. Operator error in manual log management can also contribute to missing entries. Resolve by renewing the certificate and conducting a full access review to verify permission integrity. Educate the customer on proper log retention policies and secure credential management to prevent recurrence.

title: Permission Engine Certificate Expiration Handling
content_summary: Steps to resolve account lockouts and privilege anomalies caused by unpropagated credential rotations or expired certificates.
content_body: Certificate warnings and unexpected account lockouts in the Permission Engine often indicate that credential rotations have not been propagated across all nodes. Operator error during manual certificate updates is a frequent root cause. The fix requires performing a fresh credential rotation and ensuring the configuration change is pushed to all service instances. Finally, complete an access review to confirm that elevated privileges have been correctly normalized.

title: Diagnosing RBAC and Conditional Access Failures
content_summary: Broad troubleshooting for HTTP 401s, incorrect role applications, and tenant data visibility issues in MFA Manager.
content_body: When users encounter HTTP 401 errors or see incorrect tenant data, investigate policy misconfigurations in RBAC rules. Operator errors in setting conditional access blocks often lead to unexpected permission denials or improper privilege elevation. Start by reviewing the effective permissions for the affected user group. Correct the policy configuration and update permissions as needed, then educate the admin on proper role assignment procedures to avoid future mismatches.

title: Duplicate Tickets: Browser Inconsistency and Crash Reports
content_summary: Handling duplicate tickets regarding cross-browser inconsistencies and crashes where root cause is initially unclear.
content_body: Duplicate tickets citing inconsistent browser behavior or application crashes often lack sufficient information for immediate root cause analysis. Verify if the reporter has already provided detailed logs; if not, request specific browser versions and reproduction steps. In many cases, these are operator errors in configuration or unknown edge cases. Escalate to engineering for deeper analysis if patterns emerge, and ensure the customer is educated on gathering proper diagnostic data.

title: Currency Converter Data Corruption and Encoding Issues
content_summary: Resolving encoding errors and duplicate records resulting from data migration defects or quality issues.
content_body: Encoding errors and duplicate records in the Currency Converter are typically caused by defects during data migration or underlying data quality issues. Identify the affected ranges and run a diagnostic script to pinpoint the encoding mismatch. Use a data repair script or initiate a full data re-sync to clean up the corrupted entries. Manual reconciliation may be required for complex transactions, followed by a review of the migration process to prevent recurrence.

title: High Latency and Timeouts Under Load
content_summary: Investigating slow mobile performance and timeouts caused by database contention or capacity limits.
content_body: When mobile app performance slows or timeouts occur under load, check for database contention issues first. Capacity limitations in the backend infrastructure are also common culprits during traffic spikes. Resolve by optimizing database queries and indexes to reduce lock times. If the system is genuinely under-provisioned, request a capacity increase. Monitor latency metrics to confirm the optimization has reduced response times to acceptable levels.

title: Resolving Database Deadlocks and Replication Lag in Secret Store
content_summary: Guidance for addressing database deadlocks and high replication lag in Secret Store and Webhook Engine caused by capacity limits or hardware failure.
content_body: When agents report slow responses alongside database deadlock alerts, check the underlying infrastructure health first. Capacity limitations often trigger these deadlocks under heavy load. If hardware failure is suspected, initiate an immediate failover to a healthy node. Subsequently, request a capacity increase to prevent recurrence and schedule the failed hardware for replacement.

title: Attribution Engine Report Delays and Mobile Latency
content_summary: Troubleshooting steps for slow mobile app performance and report generation delays in Attribution Engine linked to resource exhaustion.
content_body: Report generation delays often correlate with high latency in mobile clients due to backend resource exhaustion. Monitor database contention metrics during peak reporting windows. Optimizing complex queries can reduce immediate load, but a capacity increase is usually required for sustained performance. Adjust rate limits on the API gateway if specific endpoints are being hammered by clients.

title: Handling Third-Party Outages and Notification Failures
content_summary: Broad guidelines for managing upstream dependency timeouts and SMS/notification failures caused by vendor outages or configuration errors.
content_body: When notifications fail or upstream timeouts occur, verify the vendor's status page for active incidents. Expired API keys or clock synchronization issues are common internal causes for these errors. Rotate credentials immediately if authentication errors persist. For confirmed vendor outages, engage the vendor's support team and apply local workarounds such as queuing failed requests for retry.

title: Config Manager Form Submission Failures and Blank Screens
content_summary: Fixes for white screens and missing localization text during form submissions in Config Manager, often due to stale cache or defects.
content_body: Users encountering blank screens or missing text during form submissions should first clear their browser cache. If the issue persists across multiple users, suspect a product defect in the localization module. Apply a known workaround if available in the release notes. If no workaround exists, escalate to engineering with screenshots and network logs from the failed submission.

title: Compliance Violations in Wallet Service and Tax Calculator
content_summary: Addressing data residency flags, missing consent records, and audit log gaps in compliance-sensitive products.
content_body: Incomplete compliance reports or missing consent records often stem from operator errors or unsupported configurations. Review the audit logs for gaps in data residency enforcement. Implement additional monitoring alerts to catch retention policy violations early. Conduct an access review to ensure only authorized personnel are modifying these settings, and educate operators on correct configuration procedures.

title: LDAP Connector Federation and MFA Issues
content_summary: Resolving SSO errors and MFA rejections in LDAP Connector caused by expired certificates or misconfiguration.
content_body: If users report MFA prompts not appearing or SSO errors, check the expiration date on the federation certificates. An expired certificate will break the trust relationship with the identity provider. Renew the certificate and update the connector configuration. Verify that the operator has correctly mapped the user attributes to prevent subsequent login failures.

title: Stuck Provisioning and Duplicate Accounts in Onboarding Wizard
content_summary: Steps to resolve stuck syncs and duplicate account creation caused by dependency failures or data quality issues.
content_body: Provisioning stalls often indicate a failure in an upstream dependency or poor data quality in the source system. Run a data repair script to clean up malformed entries that are blocking the queue. Manually reconcile any duplicate accounts created during the glitch. If the root cause is a third-party service outage, engage the vendor and pause automated retries to prevent further errors.

title: Webhook Engine High Latency and Slow Page Loads
content_summary: Mitigating intermittent failures and slow responses in Webhook Engine due to database contention and resource exhaustion.
content_body: High latency in webhook delivery can degrade page load times for dependent services. Investigate database contention metrics to identify long-running transactions. Increase instance capacity to handle traffic spikes more effectively. Consider optimizing database indexes or adjusting rate limits to smooth out burst traffic patterns.

title: Customer Portal Failover and Pod Restart Issues
content_summary: Legacy guidance for resolving failover failures and repeating pod restarts caused by dependency issues and resource exhaustion.
content_body: When the Customer Portal experiences partial outages and pods fail to restart, check the health of dependent services. Resource exhaustion often prevents failover mechanisms from triggering correctly. In older deployments, manual intervention was required to adjust rate limits and restart the affected pods. Ensure capacity is increased to stabilize the environment before re-enabling automated failover rules.

title: Token Expiration and MFA Rejection in SSO
content_summary: Troubleshooting MFA code rejections and SSO errors related to token expiration in identity providers.
content_body: If MFA codes are consistently rejected despite correct entry, verify the validity of the underlying authentication tokens. Expired certificates or misconfigured token lifetimes can cause these silent failures. Renew the relevant certificates and review the token issuance logs. Educate administrators on the proper sequence for rotating keys to avoid service disruption.

title: Handling Duplicate Tickets with Inconsistent Behavior Reports
content_summary: Guidance on closing duplicate tickets when initial reports of browser inconsistencies or crashes lack sufficient detail for root cause analysis.
content_body: When multiple tickets are filed for the same issue involving inconsistent browser behavior or application crashes, verify if the new ticket provides unique logs or reproduction steps. If the information is insufficient to determine a root cause distinct from an existing open case, link the new ticket to the primary case. Close the duplicate ticket as 'Operator Error' or 'Insufficient Information' to maintain workflow hygiene. Ensure the primary ticket is updated with any additional context provided in the duplicate report before closing.

title: Troubleshooting Billing Discrepancies and Failed Payments in Subscription Manager
content_summary: Broad overview of common billing issues including payment declines, double charges, and currency conversion errors within Subscription Manager.
content_body: Billing discrepancies in Subscription Manager often stem from third-party payment gateway failures, operator configuration errors, or product defects. Begin by checking the transaction logs for specific error codes related to declined payments or incorrect currency conversions. If the issue affects multiple customers with similar configurations, escalate to engineering for a potential product patch. For isolated incidents, verify that proration settings and invoice generation rules are correctly configured. Engage the payment vendor if the root cause appears to be external to our platform.

title: Addressing Capacity Limits and Autoscaling Failures in Deploy Manager
content_summary: Specific steps to resolve issues where capacity limits are reached or autoscaling fails to trigger due to misconfigurations or resource exhaustion.
content_body: If autoscaling is not triggering as expected, first check the current resource utilization metrics to confirm if the threshold has actually been met. Verify that rate limit configurations are not incorrectly blocking scaling actions or API requests to the scaling service. In cases of resource exhaustion, review the capacity planning gaps and adjust the maximum instance count or memory limits accordingly. A configuration change to the rate limits or scaling policies is typically required to resolve these issues.

title: Resolving Configuration Drift and Missing Environment Variables in Funnel Analyzer
content_summary: General guidance for troubleshooting services that are unresponsive or exhibit data mismatches due to template misconfigurations or incorrect environment variables.
content_body: Configuration drift in Funnel Analyzer often results from unsupported configuration values or policy misconfigurations that prevent changes from taking effect. Check for missing environment variables that may cause the service to fail silently or return stale data. If feature flags are not applying, verify that the configuration source is correctly linked and that there are no conflicting settings. Customer education on proper template management and documentation corrections for ambiguous settings are common resolutions.

title: Fixing Refund Processing Failures and Overcharges in Invoice Service
content_summary: Specific troubleshooting for refunds that are not processed or result in overcharges, often linked to customer configuration errors or known product defects.
content_body: When refunds fail to process or result in unexpected overcharges in Invoice Service, first validate the customer's refund configuration and currency settings. If the configuration is correct, check for known product defects affecting currency conversion or payment gateway interactions. Apply the known-issue workaround if available, which may involve manually adjusting the invoice before re-triggering the refund. For persistent issues, a configuration change or product patch may be required to correct the underlying logic.

title: Compliance Report Gaps and Retention Policy Issues in Status Page
content_summary: Explanation of why compliance reports may be incomplete or retention policies not applied, focusing on known limitations and operator errors.
content_body: Incomplete compliance reports in Status Page are frequently caused by known product limitations regarding data residency flags or retention policy scopes. Verify if the configuration aligns with the supported retention windows and data residency requirements. Operator error in setting up the initial compliance rules is another common cause; review the configuration against the documentation. If the behavior matches known limitations, provide customer education on the current scope and apply any available workarounds.

title: Session Expiration and MFA Issues in Permission Engine and Token Service
content_summary: Troubleshooting HTTP 401 errors, expired password reset links, and rejected MFA codes related to token handling bugs or unsupported configurations.
content_body: Users experiencing HTTP 401 errors or rejected MFA codes should check the session expiration settings in Permission Engine. A token expiration handling bug in Token Service can cause premature session termination or invalid tokens. Verify if the current configuration is supported for the specific authentication flow being used. Resolutions often involve a token/session reset for the affected user, configuration changes to adjust expiration times, or applying a product patch if a bug is confirmed.

title: Certificate Expiration Warnings and Account Lockouts in Data Pipeline
content_summary: Steps to resolve account lockouts and certificate warnings caused by expired credentials or propagation delays in Data Pipeline.
content_body: Certificate warnings in Data Pipeline often indicate that credential rotation has not propagated fully to all dependent services. If accounts are locked out, check if the associated certificates have expired or if the rotation schedule was missed. Operator error in scheduling rotations or updating trust stores is a common root cause. The typical resolution involves performing a manual credential rotation and verifying the configuration change in the pipeline settings.

title: Third-Party Dependencies and Notification Failures in Notification Hub
content_summary: Broad overview of issues like SMS failures, timeouts, or undelivered notifications stemming from vendor outages, deprecated APIs, or expired keys.
content_body: Notification failures in Notification Hub are frequently linked to third-party service degradation, deprecated vendor APIs, or expired API keys. Check the vendor's status page for active incidents if timeouts or delivery failures are reported. Verify that API keys are current and that the integration uses supported endpoints. If the vendor is at fault, engage them directly; otherwise, rotate credentials or apply a workaround for deprecated API changes.

title: Service Outages and Health Check Failures in Secret Store and Rate Limiter
content_summary: Guidance for troubleshooting degraded availability, 503 errors, and failover failures caused by resource exhaustion or dependency issues.
content_body: When Secret Store or Rate Limiter services return 503 errors or fail health checks, investigate resource exhaustion and container OOMKilled events. Failover mechanisms may not trigger if a race condition or dependency failure blocks the secondary instance from starting. Engage engineering to analyze logs for race conditions or dependency remediation needs. Increasing capacity or adjusting rate limits are common immediate resolutions to restore availability while a product patch is developed.

title: Fixing Webhook Engine Connectivity: Expired Certificates and Routing Issues
content_summary: Specific guidance for Webhook Engine timeouts and connection refusals caused by expired certificates or network routing errors. Details steps for certificate renewal and load balancer reconfiguration.
content_body: Check the expiration date of the TLS certificate used by the Webhook Engine endpoint and renew it immediately if expired. If connections are refused, verify that the network routing configuration allows traffic to the designated port and IP. Review firewall rules to ensure they are not blocking inbound webhook requests. If the issue is related to load balancing, reconfigure the load balancer to distribute traffic correctly among healthy nodes. Confirm that the updated certificate is deployed across all instances before testing connectivity.

title: Troubleshooting Fee Analyzer Connectivity: TLS, Proxy, and Network Partitions
content_summary: Addresses connectivity issues in Fee Analyzer, including certificate warnings, DNS failures, and connection resets. Provides steps for renewing certificates, correcting DNS, and updating firewall rules.
content_body: If users see certificate warnings, verify that the SSL certificate is valid and properly installed on the server. For DNS lookup failures, check the resolver configuration and ensure it can reach the authoritative nameservers. Connection resets often indicate firewall misconfigurations or network partitions; review security group rules and network ACLs. If a proxy is involved, ensure it is correctly forwarding traffic and not modifying headers unexpectedly. Apply DNS corrections and firewall rule updates to resolve the underlying connectivity barriers.

title: Admin Console: Intermittent 503 Errors and Failed Health Checks
content_summary: Investigate intermittent 5xx errors in the Admin Console where health checks fail and automatic failover does not trigger, often caused by race conditions or dependency failures.
content_body: Check the Admin Console logs for 503 responses coinciding with health check failures. If failover did not occur, investigate if a specific backend dependency was unavailable during the window. A known race condition in the health-check probe may prevent the load balancer from marking the node as unhealthy; apply the latest product patch to resolve this. If the root cause is an external dependency failure, engage engineering for escalation and coordinate with the vendor for remediation.

title: Role Manager: Delayed Permission Propagation and Access Denied Errors
content_summary: Troubleshoot issues where new roles or permissions are not applied immediately in Role Manager, resulting in access denied errors or incorrect access levels.
content_body: When users report 'access denied' despite having the correct role assigned, check for propagation delays in the Role Manager cache. This is often caused by a customer configuration error in the sync interval or a policy misconfiguration that prevents immediate updates. Verify that the user's token was issued after the role change; if not, force a token refresh. Educate customers that changes may take several minutes to propagate and review documentation on manual cache invalidation steps.

title: Legacy Upgrade Path: Config Manager and Load Balancer Version Incompatibility
content_summary: Addresses deployment failures and migration script errors when upgrading Config Manager and Load Balancer components, specifically noting version incompatibilities in older release cycles.
content_body: If a deployment fails after upgrading Config Manager, check the Load Balancer version compatibility matrix for the specific release. Migration script errors often occur when the Load Balancer is running an older major version than required by the new Config Manager build. Prior to the introduction of the automated compatibility checker, manual verification was required; if a bad deployment is detected, immediately rollback to the previous stable version. Apply the available product patch for the specific version gap or perform a coordinated version upgrade for both components.

title: Chat Widget: Troubleshooting Third-Party API Timeouts and Delivery Failures
content_summary: General guidance for resolving Chat Widget issues stemming from upstream rate limiting, deprecated APIs, or expired credentials, including SMS and notification delivery failures.
content_body: When Chat Widget notifications, SMS, or file uploads fail, check for timeout errors or 429 status codes indicating upstream rate limiting. Verify that the API keys for third-party dependencies have not expired and that the endpoint versions are not deprecated. If a dependency version conflict is suspected, review recent integration changes. Common resolutions include rotating credentials, implementing a workaround for rate limits, or engaging the vendor for API status updates.

title: Queue Manager: Autoscaling Failures and Resource Exhaustion During Scale-Down
content_summary: Investigate cases where Queue Manager autoscaling does not trigger correctly or CPU spikes occur, potentially leading to data loss during scale-down events due to misconfigured limits.
content_body: Check if the Queue Manager metrics show a capacity limit reached without triggering an autoscaling event. This is often caused by a rate limit misconfiguration in the autoscaler policy or resource exhaustion on the host nodes. If data loss is observed during a scale-down event, verify that the graceful shutdown timeout is sufficient for active jobs to complete. Adjust the rate limits and request a capacity increase if the current infrastructure cannot support the workload profile.

title: Config Manager: Performance Degradation, Slow Reports, and Database Timeouts
content_summary: Broad troubleshooting for Config Manager performance issues, including slow page loads, batch job delays, and database query timeouts caused by resource exhaustion or third-party failures.
content_body: For slow response times or high latency in Config Manager, first check database query logs for timeouts and monitor CPU usage spikes. Batch job slowness may indicate resource exhaustion or a race condition in the processing queue. If third-party services are involved, verify their availability to rule out external dependency failures. Resolutions may include applying a product patch, increasing capacity, adjusting rate limits, or escalating to engineering for complex race conditions.

title: Permission Engine: Conditional Access Blocks and HTTP 401 Errors
content_summary: Troubleshoot access denied errors and HTTP 401 responses in Permission Engine caused by conditional access policies blocking valid users or displaying wrong tenant data.
content_body: When users receive HTTP 401 errors or report that wrong tenant data is shown, review the active conditional access policies in Permission Engine. Operator error in defining policy conditions or incorrect permission assignments can inadvertently block legitimate access. Perform a targeted access review to identify the specific rule causing the block. Correct the policy configuration and update permissions to ensure the user's context matches the expected access requirements.

title: Legacy Dependency Issues: Help Center and Config Manager API Timeouts
content_summary: Guidance for resolving third-party API unavailability and timeout issues in Help Center and Config Manager, often stemming from older dependency versions or clock synchronization problems.
content_body: If Help Center or Config Manager reports upstream dependency errors or timeouts, check for clock synchronization issues between the application server and the third-party API gateway. Older versions of these integrations were sensitive to time drift, causing signature validation failures. Verify that the dependency license and version are compatible with the current vendor API requirements. Common resolutions include remediating the dependency, adjusting configuration for time sync, or engaging the vendor if the service itself is down.

title: Wallet Service: Account Lockouts and Missing Audit Logs from Expired Certificates
content_summary: Investigate unexpected logouts, account lockouts, and missing audit entries in Wallet Service, which may be caused by expired certificates or improper access reviews in older security models.
content_body: Check for missing entries in the audit log alongside unexpected user logouts in Wallet Service. This behavior was often caused by expired client certificates that triggered security blocks before logging could occur. Review the certificate expiration status and ensure access reviews are completed for all service principals. Renew any expired certificates and update permissions to prevent future lockouts; note that the new security model handles these events differently.

title: Unclassified Issues: Intermittent Failures and Data Mismatches
content_summary: General approach for handling tickets with intermittent, unreproducible symptoms such as slow responses, crashes, or inconsistent browser behavior where root cause is unclear.
content_body: When facing intermittent failures, data mismatches, or application crashes without a clear pattern, first verify that the configuration is supported. Lack of information often prevents immediate root cause determination; request detailed logs, browser console outputs, and reproduction steps. If the issue appears to be operator error, provide customer education on correct usage patterns. For persistent, unexplained issues, escalate to engineering for deeper analysis and conduct an access review if data discrepancies are suspected.
